question.problem:
The weekly exercise time for a community is normally distributed with a mean of $\mu $ minutes and a standard deviation of $30$ minutes. Additionally, $60%$ of people exercise between $0.9\mu $ minutes and $1.1\mu $ minutes each week. Find the percentage of people who exercise less than $220$ minutes per week. **Round your answer to two decimal places.**

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $p$ | $\,0.75\,$ | $\,0.80\,$ | $\,0.85\,$ | $\,0.90\,$ | $\,0.95\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,0.6745\,$ | $\,0.8416\,$ | $\,1.0364\,$ | $\,1.2816\,$ | $\,1.6449\,$ |

$$

$$

*In addition, you're given the following table of values for $p=Φ(z)$*.

| $z$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ | $\,0.09\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-1.2\,$ | $\,0.1020\,$ | $\,0.1003\,$ | $\,0.0985\,$ |
| $\,-1.1\,$ | $\,0.1210\,$ | $\,0.1190\,$ | $\,0.1170\,$ |
| $\,-1.0\,$ | $\,0.1423\,$ | $\,0.1401\,$ | $\,0.1379\,$ |

Approximately
{{field-1}}$%$ of the people exercise less than $220$ minutes per week.
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the weekly exercise time of a randomly selected person. Then we have $X∼N(\mu ,{30}^{2}),$ and we want to find $P(X<220).$ But first, we need to find the mean $\mu .$ 

We know that $P(0.9\mu <X<1.1\mu )=0.60.$ First, we convert this to a cumulative probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.9\mu <X<1.1\mu ) & =0.60 \\ 2P(\mu <X<1.1\mu ) & =0.60 \\ P(\mu <X<1.1\mu ) & =0.30 \\ P(X<\mu )+P(\mu <X<1.1\mu ) & =0.5+0.30 \\ P(X<1.1\mu ) & =0.80\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<1.1\mu ) & =0.80 \\ P(Z<\frac{0.1\mu }{30}) & =0.80 \\ Φ(\frac{0.1\mu }{30}) & =0.80 \\ \frac{0.1\mu }{30} & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.80).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, 

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.80)=0.8416.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{0.1\mu }{30} & =0.8416 \\ 0.1\mu  & =25.248 \\ \mu  & =\frac{25.248}{0.1} \\  & ≈252.48.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can solve for $P(X<220)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<220) & =P(Z<\frac{220-252.48}{30}) \\  & ≈P(Z<-1.08) \\  & =Φ(-1.08) \\  & =0.1401 \\  & ≈14.01%\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, approximately $14.01%$ of the people exercise less than $220$ minutes per week.
